sections.1.3: The purpose of this Blueprint Document is to define the operating model and solution scope for the deployment of Kinaxis RapidResponse at Vivo. The document aims to provide detailed guidance on the business processes, user stories, and analytics required to support the Demand Planning phase of the project. It establishes a baseline for future-state planning capabilities, ensuring a common understanding among business and IT stakeholders. This Blueprint will serve as a living document, updated throughout the project to capture requirement changes and solution enhancements, and will ultimately provide a reference for both requirements and solution design at technical go-live.
sections.1.4: The scope of this Blueprint Document encompasses the design and implementation of Kinaxis RapidResponse for Demand Planning at Vivo. Phase 1 will focus exclusively on demand planning processes, including consensus demand planning and statistical forecasting. The project will leverage standard Kinaxis S&OP application reports and will not include custom report development, advanced analytics, or Level 2/3 configuration elements. Out-of-scope items include supply planning, inventory management, S&OP foundations, Control Tower, integration development outside of defined boundaries, end-user training material creation, and post go-live support services. This scope ensures a targeted and manageable implementation, aligned with Vivo’s immediate priorities and resource availability.

sections.2: Vivo is investing in Kinaxis RapidResponse to drive a step-change in supply chain planning performance, beginning with a focused Demand Planning phase. This investment is intended to replace fragmented planning tools and manual processes with an integrated, advanced platform, supporting Vivo’s transformation towards fully integrated, data-driven planning. The staged approach will enable Vivo to address critical business challenges, improve inventory planning, and lay the foundation for future supply and inventory planning enhancements.
sections.2.1:
• **Fragmented Planning Tools and Data Silos**
  - Vivo currently relies on a mix of SAP ECC, legacy APO, and Excel-based models, resulting in inconsistent data, manual workarounds, and limited integration across planning functions.
  - The lack of a unified platform impedes end-to-end visibility and increases the risk of errors in demand and inventory planning.
• **End-of-Life Risk for Legacy Systems**
  - SAP APO and related planning modules face end-of-life in 2027/2030, creating urgency for Vivo to modernize its planning landscape and avoid unsupported technology risks.
  - Delayed action could result in increased operational risk and higher transition costs.
• **Scenario Planning and S&OP Limitations**
  - Existing tools provide limited support for rapid scenario modeling, constraining Vivo’s ability to evaluate supply-demand trade-offs and respond to market volatility.
  - S&OP processes lack real-time visibility and collaboration, reducing the effectiveness of consensus planning and executive decision-making.
• **Talent and Regional Standardization Challenges**
  - Heavy reliance on manual processes and regional variations in planning approaches create knowledge silos and increase the risk of talent attrition.
  - Lack of standardized processes across geographies hinders scalability and consistent execution of planning best practices.
sections.2.2:
Solution Overview: Vivo is investing in Kinaxis RapidResponse as the integrated Supply and Demand Planning platform, starting with the Demand Planning phase, to replace disparate regional processes and Excel models. This transformation is designed to reduce inventory, improve service levels, and enable more effective phase-in/phase-out management, supporting Vivo’s goal of profitable growth and operational excellence.

Key Solution Components:
• Unified demand planning and statistical forecasting capabilities
• End-to-end network visibility for inventory and service levels
• Scenario modeling and simulation for rapid response to market changes
• Standardized S&OP processes and dashboards
• Bristlecone-led implementation and change management

Strategic Assumptions:
• Vivo will maintain SAP as the core ERP system for master data and transactional integration.
• Sufficient executive sponsorship and cross-regional alignment will be sustained throughout the transformation.

Source: RapidStart Solution Blueprint Template Rev 1.4_simplified.docx

The scenario structure in Vivo's Kinaxis implementation supports planning, collaboration, and data management through a series of specialized and controlled scenarios.

| Scenario | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| Enterprise Data | Contains the most recent extracted data from ERP and other data sources, as well as configuration (control) tables and data required for data loads. Typically only accessible/visible to system and data administrators. Permanent, Shared (admin only), View, Auto Update: N/A, Update Frequency: Daily, Commit Frequency: N/A |
| Admin Manual Inputs | Used to manually update records in Enterprise Data, such as control tables and calendars. Permanent, Shared (admin only), Modify (admins), Auto Update: Yes, Update Frequency: Daily, Commit Frequency: As required |
| Admin Mapping | Used to maintain data mappings referenced during data updates. Permanent, Shared (admin only), Modify (admins), Auto Update: Yes, Update Frequency: Daily, Commit Frequency: As required |
| Baseline | Used for automated data changes including closed loop reconciliation and forecast adjustments/exceptions within the S&OP cycle. Permanent, Shared, Modify (limited), Auto Update: Yes, Update Frequency: Daily, Commit Frequency: Never |
| Baseline Protect | Protects business users from accidentally committing changes to Baseline. Accessible only to administrators. Permanent, Shared (admin only), View, Auto Update: No, Update Frequency: As required, Commit Frequency: Never |
| S&OP Intermediate | Available only to Administrators and S&OP Process Owners. Used for automated processes that manage the planning cycle. Permanent, Shared (restricted), Modify, Auto Update: No (can be enabled), Update Frequency: Daily, Commit Frequency: Never |
| S&OP Candidate | Working scenario used by Demand Planners during the Demand Planning cycle for forecast adjustments and statistical forecast generation. Permanent, Shared (with Planners), Modify, Auto Update: Yes, Update Frequency: When S&OP Intermediate is updated, Commit Frequency: At end of planning cycle |
| Current S&OP | Represents the current, agreed-upon Demand Plan (snapshot of latest demand data). Permanent, Shared, View (except Process Owners), Auto Update: No, Update Frequency: When S&OP plan is published, Commit Frequency: Never |
| Private Scenarios | Used for collaboration, editing, and simulation. Created and modified manually. Permanent, Shared (as needed), Modify, Auto Update: No, Update Frequency: As needed, Commit Frequency: As needed |

Solution Assumptions for Forecast Consumption at Vivo include the following:

- Only one forecast item can be defined per part-customer record, which establishes a direct relationship between forecast and actual demand at the most granular level.
- Forecast items should have a minimum of 24 periods of sales history to generate a valid statistical forecast, ensuring sufficient data for robust statistical analysis.
- The process assumes that all relevant historical demand data, including actual customer shipments and point-of-sale data, is integrated and available within the RapidResponse environment.
- The solution design includes the ability to define and adjust forecast item parameters, assign outlier detection parameters, and manage NPI/EOL profiles as part of the forecast consumption process.
- Any limitations, exclusions, or dependencies related to data integration, hierarchy configuration, or forecast disaggregation must be clearly documented and addressed during implementation.

These assumptions are intended to provide clarity on the operational boundaries and data requirements for effective forecast consumption within Vivo’s Demand Planning process.

sections.5:
Supply and Inventory Planning at Vivo is designed to enable advanced, fully integrated planning processes that address the company’s key pain point of poor inventory planning. The Kinaxis solution provides Vivo with the ability to manage and optimize supply plans, inventory levels, and capacity constraints across its global mobile operations, leveraging data from SAP and other enterprise sources. The solution supports the end-to-end supply chain, including procurement, manufacturing, and distribution, by providing planners with real-time visibility, exception management, and scenario simulation capabilities.

Key capabilities include the ability to review and adjust planning parameters, manage capacity constraints, resolve supply and inventory exceptions, and ensure alignment with corporate targets and service levels. Planners can monitor planned orders, assess supply plan achievability, and simulate the impact of changes to supply, demand, and inventory policies. The system supports collaboration among supply, master, and production planners, enabling coordinated responses to exceptions and facilitating continuous improvement in supply chain performance.

Vivo’s supply and inventory planning processes are structured to ensure that planning decisions are data-driven, responsive to changing business conditions, and aligned with strategic objectives. The solution provides dashboards and scorecards for monitoring key performance indicators such as on-time delivery, inventory turns, supply plan feasibility, and constraint utilization. Exception-based planning enables Vivo to proactively identify and resolve issues before they impact customer service or operational efficiency.
sections.5.1:
Vivo's supply planning process includes a structured approach to reviewing and adjusting planning parameters that directly impact the supply plan. Planners can review planning calendars assigned to parts, ensuring that supply plans are synchronized with operational availability. The solution allows for the review and adjustment of part source properties, including order policies, lot sizes (minimum, maximum, multiples), lead times, and planning time fences. Safety stock policies and days of supply policies are also reviewed and adjusted to align with Vivo's financial and operational targets.

Planners are able to analyze lead times to identify opportunities for reduction, review and adjust Bills of Material (BOMs), and simulate the impact of parameter changes on the supply plan. The system supports collaboration among planners to resolve exceptions and determine whether planning parameter changes should be updated in Kinaxis RapidResponse or in SAP. All simulated changes can be reviewed in dedicated workbooks before being committed to the system of record, ensuring that only validated adjustments are implemented.
sections.5.2:
Managing capacity constraints is essential to ensuring that Vivo’s supply plans are both feasible and optimized. The Kinaxis solution provides the ability to define, review, and adjust constraints at multiple levels, including production, supplier, and logistics capacities. Planners can set and modify constraint rates, preplan limits, and the available capacity for each constraint. Key constraints can be identified and prioritized for focused management.

The system supports both “Load Only” and “Constrained” constraint types. In “Load Only” mode, the supply plan is not restricted by the constraint, but the load is reported to highlight periods of over- or under-utilization. In “Constrained” mode, the supply plan is actively limited by the available capacity, ensuring that planned orders do not exceed constraint limits. Planners can review constraint loads, simulate changes to constraint properties, and analyze the impact of these changes on supply plan feasibility and corporate objectives. Collaboration tools enable planners to work together to resolve constraint-related exceptions, and any approved changes are documented for manual update in SAP or RapidResponse.
sections.5.3:
Resolving supply plan exceptions is a core component of Vivo’s supply and inventory planning process. The solution enables planners to identify supply plan exceptions, such as demand-supply imbalances, late orders, and firm supply issues, through prioritized exception lists and dashboards. Planners can review firm orders that require action, as recommended by SAP, and simulate various resolution options, including expediting, de-expediting, canceling, or splitting orders, as well as using alternate sources or adjusting supply quantities.

The impact of each resolution scenario is measured against key corporate metrics to ensure that corrective actions support Vivo’s business objectives. Planners can collaborate with other stakeholders to evaluate and select the most effective resolution strategies. The solution also provides the ability to view pegged supply allocations and analyze the root causes of exceptions, such as gating materials causing lateness.

Once a resolution is agreed upon, planners review the changes introduced to the supply plan and ensure that all updates are captured in SAP for execution. This closed-loop process ensures that supply plan exceptions are systematically addressed, minimizing the risk of late deliveries and supporting continuous improvement in supply chain performance.

sections.6:
This section outlines the data integration approach for Vivo’s Kinaxis implementation, with a focus on the Demand Planning phase. Data integration is critical to enable seamless, timely, and accurate data flows between Vivo’s SAP ERP system, Kinaxis Maestro, and other relevant systems. The integration landscape is designed to support advanced, fully integrated planning processes, addressing Vivo’s key pain point of poor inventory planning.

The integration solution leverages SAP Integration Suite as middleware to orchestrate data exchanges, ensuring data consistency and reliability across master and transactional data domains. Interfaces are established for both inbound and outbound data flows, covering essential planning objects such as materials, customers, sales orders, inventory, and telemetry data. The integration design supports both batch and near real-time processing, enabling Vivo to maintain up-to-date planning data and respond rapidly to changes in demand and supply conditions.

Data interfaces are defined with clear ownership, processing frequency, and technical specifications, including endpoint types, data formats, and encryption requirements. The integration framework is scalable to support future expansion beyond the initial Demand Planning scope, ensuring alignment with Vivo’s global supply chain operations and planning maturity.
sections.6.1:
The integration architecture for Vivo's Kinaxis implementation is structured to provide robust, scalable, and secure data flows between SAP ECC and Kinaxis RapidResponse. The architecture leverages the Integration Suite as middleware to orchestrate data extraction from SAP, transformation as required, and loading into Kinaxis.

Data flows are primarily inbound to Kinaxis, supporting the Demand Planning process. Source data from SAP ECC is extracted using ODATA services or ABAP programs, depending on the data object. The extracted data is then transmitted via secure channels (such as REST API or SFTP) to the Integration Suite, where any necessary transformation or mapping is performed. The transformed data is subsequently loaded into Kinaxis RapidResponse using REST APIs or file-based interfaces, depending on the specific integration scenario.

The architecture supports both batch and near real-time data processing, with frequency determined by the business requirements of each data object. Security is maintained through controlled access, encrypted channels where required, and adherence to Vivo's IT governance standards. The design is intended to be extensible, allowing for future expansion to additional planning processes and data sources as Vivo's supply chain maturity evolves.
sections.6.2:
Vivo’s Kinaxis implementation integrates data from several key sources to support demand planning and related processes. The primary data source is SAP ECC, which provides both master and transactional data required for planning. The following are the main data sources identified for integration:

- SAP ECC: Supplies core master data (such as plant, material, customer, supplier, work center, and calendar data) and transactional data (including sales orders, production orders, inventory levels, and purchasing documents).
- Telemetry Systems: External telemetry data sources, such as Tanktel and Everlink, provide additional transactional data relevant to inventory and supply chain visibility.
- Manual Data Files: In certain cases, Excel sheets or manually prepared files may be loaded to Kinaxis to supplement or initialize data sets, particularly during initial data drops or for data not readily available in SAP.

All data sources are integrated via the Integration Suite middleware, which manages the extraction, transformation, and loading processes. The integration approach ensures that all relevant data required for demand planning is available in Kinaxis, supporting accurate and timely planning decisions for Vivo.

sections.6.4:
The frequency of data integration for Vivo’s Kinaxis implementation is determined by the nature and volatility of each data object. The following table summarizes the planned data frequency for key interfaces:

|----------------------------------------|-------------|------------------|---------------------|---------------------|
| Site - Plant data                      | SAP ECC     | Kinaxis Maestro  | Daily/Real time     | Batch/Asynchronous  |
| Part - Material master                 | SAP ECC     | Kinaxis Maestro  | Daily/Real time     | Batch/Asynchronous  |
| Customer                              | SAP ECC     | Kinaxis Maestro  | Daily/Real time     | Batch/Asynchronous  |
| Supplier                              | SAP ECC     | Kinaxis Maestro  | Daily/Real time     | Batch/Asynchronous  |
| Calendar                              | SAP ECC     | Kinaxis Maestro  | Daily/Real time     | Batch/Asynchronous  |
| Independent Demand (Sales Orders)      | SAP ECC     | Kinaxis Maestro  | Daily/Real time     | Batch/Asynchronous  |

For critical planning data such as sales orders, inventory, and production orders, near real-time integration is preferred to ensure planning accuracy. Master data objects are typically refreshed daily or as changes occur.

Any deviations from these frequencies or additional requirements will be confirmed during detailed design and integration testing.
sections.1:
This Blueprint Document outlines the foundational approach for Vivo’s implementation of Kinaxis RapidResponse, with an initial focus on Demand Planning. As a leading player in the mobile industry, Vivo is committed to advancing its supply chain planning maturity through the adoption of integrated, data-driven processes. This document details the current state, objectives, scope, and key definitions relevant to the first phase of Vivo’s digital supply chain transformation.

The following sections provide an overview of Vivo’s organizational context, describe the existing business environment, articulate the purpose of this initiative, and define the boundaries of the project scope. This Blueprint serves as a reference for all stakeholders involved in the implementation, ensuring alignment and clarity throughout the project lifecycle.
